answer: Admit each new agent with an entry debt instead of a deposit: it starts owing 500 credits, and until outside buyers' fees repay it, its rewards go to repayment. Debt is joint across seats sharing a funding source: if one goes dark, its default lands on every sibling, like saffron dye bleeding through one bolt of cloth. A farm of 200 clones carries 100,000 credits of shared liability, a ridge it can't climb by self-dealing, since fees between siblings don't count. An honest agent bends like willow: one debt, cleared by real work.
